quick_skim.title: Region-Weighted Losses and Model Fusion for Cross-Modal PET Attenuation Correction
quick_skim.abstract: We describe our approach to the Big Cross-Modal Attenuation Correction (BIC-MAC) challenge, which asks for a pseudo-CT in Hounsfield Units to be synthesized from Non-Attenuation-Corrected PET (NAC-PET), DIXON MRI and a topogram, and scores both the pseudo-CT and the Attenuation-Corrected PET (AC-PET) reconstructed from it. Three ideas carried our improvements over the organizers' 3D U-Net baseline. The loss matters more than the architecture: we compute the $L_1$ error in the Carney attenuation-coefficient ($μ$) space that the CT metric itself uses, weighted by anatomical region. Only once that loss was in place did the unregistered DIXON MRI work as extra input channels. A fixed convex combination of two independently trained models then beat both of its members on three of the four metrics and ranks first overall on the public validation leaderboard.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: The paper describes a loss-centric approach to PET attenuation correction, weighting L1 error in attenuation-coefficient space by anatomical region and fusing two independently trained models.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 该论文介绍了参加跨模态PET衰减校正挑战赛的方法，强调损失函数比网络结构更重要。作者在衰减系数空间中按解剖区域加权L1损失，从而让未配准的DIXON MRI能作为额外输入通道提升效果，并采用两个独立训练模型的固定凸组合进一步提升性能。结果显示该方法优于组织者提供的3D U-Net基线，为医学影像跨模态合成提供了实用的训练策略。

quick_skim.title: From Reasoning to Pixels: Grounded Medical Multimodal LLMs for VQA and Segmentation
quick_skim.abstract: Although Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have demonstrated impressive performance in Medical Visual Question Answering (Med-VQA), their reliance on global image features often lacks precise pixel-level grounding, thereby limiting clinical trustworthiness. To bridge the semantic gap between high-level clinical reasoning and spatial localization, we propose \textsc{\textsc{MedREAL}} (\textbf{Med}ical \textbf{RE}asoning-driven \textbf{A}nswering and \textbf{L}ocalization), a unified framework that seamlessly aligns linguistic reasoning with spatial grounding. Specifically, \textsc{MedREAL} introduces \textbf{S}eg \textbf{A}nchored \textbf{R}easoning \textbf{P}ooling (SARP) to distill task-relevant semantic evidence directly from \texttt{[SEG]} tokens within the MLLM's hidden states. Furthermore, a \textbf{R}easoning-to-\textbf{V}isual (R2V) fusion mechanism is proposed to effectively inject these reasoning-aware features into a segmentation pipeline for accurate mask decoding. To facilitate this paradigm, we construct MedRAVS-13K, a comprehensive dataset comprising 13,824 expertly validated samples across four diverse imaging modalities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that \textsc{MedREAL} significantly outperforms state-of-the-arts, achieving 68.49\% gIoU and 70.47\% cIoU on benchmark evaluations. By generating evidence masks that are strictly consistent with textual diagnoses, \textsc{MedREAL} provides a robust, interpretable framework for reasoning-driven medical image analysis.

quick_skim.llm_tldr_en: MedREAL aligns linguistic reasoning with spatial grounding for medical VQA and segmentation via segmentation-anchored reasoning pooling, improving clinical trustworthiness; relevant to medical multimodal LLM though not RLHF/GRPO.
quick_skim.llm_tldr_cn: 医疗多模态大语言模型在医学视觉问答中虽表现优异，但常只利用全局图像特征，缺乏像素级定位，限制了临床可信度。该文提出MedREAL框架，通过分割锚定的推理池化（SARP）从分割特征中提炼任务相关证据，将高层临床推理与空间定位对齐，统一支持VQA和分割。实验表明该框架能有效弥合推理与像素之间的语义鸿沟。虽然未涉及强化微调，但其医疗多模态理解与诊断辅助能力可作为RL后训练方法的重要基础。
